title: Nvidia's Private-Company Holdings Soar to $65.5 Billion: AI Venture Capital Trends Face Major Uncertainty After Jensen Huang's Departure

content_html:
The investment landscape of AI chip giant Nvidia is once again sending shockwaves through the industry. According to the latest TechCrunch report, Nvidia's latest disclosures show that the value of its stakes in private startups has surged to $6.55 billion (the equivalent of several tens of billions of RMB at current exchange rates), a sharp increase from the $2.2 billion reported in January this year. This asset expansion is due both to the company's recent large-scale new investments and to significant jumps in the valuations of companies in its existing portfolio.

Investment Scale Surges Against the Trend: Equity Investment Reaches $5.8 Billion in the First Nine Months

In terms of absolute capital deployed, Nvidia injected $1.6 billion into various equity investments in the past fiscal quarter alone; in the first nine months of this fiscal year, its total equity investment amount reached an astonishing $5.8 billion.

This figure not only covers stock purchases in some public and private companies, but also demonstrates that the chip giant has made unprecedentedly intensive bets on the AI ecosystem over the past year. By comparison, in the same period of the previous fiscal year (the first nine months ended November 2025), Nvidia spent only $500 million on equity acquisitions—the two levels of investment are not in the same league.

The Full Investment Map: From AI Rising Stars to Large-Scale Positioning in Infrastructure

Since late 2023, Nvidia's core goal in making enterprise-level investments has been very clear: to keep expanding the boundaries of the overall AI ecosystem by betting on what it defines as "game changers and market creators."

According to PitchBook data, over the past nearly three years, Nvidia has invested in nearly 350 startups. Its investment matrix is enormous, spanning leading large-model companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI; emerging labs such as Thinking Machines and Reflection; next-generation compute cloud providers such as Lambda, Nscale, and Cruso; and startups and application developers across AI infrastructure and robotics.
